text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The police force has been bugging all mobile phones in Turkey since 1996. Mobiles have became very popular in Turkey with the assumption that they were more protected from bugging.
- A Turkish girl, Elif Sozen, is to wed the youngest son of German Prime Minister Helmut Kohl.
- MPs from the conservative wing of the government have begun to call for an end to the coalition with the Islamist Welfare Party.
- President Suleyman Demirel is planning to hold a summit with leaders of the parties represented in the parliament amid rising tension between the Turkish armed forces and Welfare.
- An Islamist MP says the coalition has actually broken up and would officially end soon.
- Commanders of the Turkish army held a meeting to decide on issues to be discussed at the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK) meeting on March 31.

- The European Union (EU) gives Turkey time until April to change regulations that allow cheaper imports to Far Eastern car-makers that invest in Turkey because the legislation contradicts the customs union deal signed in 1995.
- Welfare mayors celebrate the third anniversary of their sweeping victory in municipal elections.
